cards.en:
Intuition: a database is a super-organised filing cabinet inside a computer. Every folder has the same labelled slots, so finding things is fast.

A database is a collection of structured data stored in a computer system that facilitates the storage and retrieval of data.

  • Structured = every record has the same fields (name, price, category...).
  • Designed to store a large amount of data efficiently.
  • Before databases: paper files → searching and sorting were slow, with a higher risk of human error.

Uses: online shops (products), schools (students), banks (transactions).

Exam wording: "A database stores structured data so that data can be searched, sorted and retrieved quickly and accurately."
cards.zh:
直觉：数据库是电脑里极有条理的文件柜：每个文件夹都有相同的标签栏位，找东西很快。

Database：存放于电脑系统、有结构的数据集合，方便储存与检索。纸本方式搜寻排序慢，且人为错误风险较高。

ex.q: A library still uses paper index cards. Give TWO benefits of a database.
ex.a:
1. Faster searching: find a book by title or author in seconds.
  2. Fewer human errors / easy sorting and updating of records.
ex.az: 1. 搜寻更快；减少人为错误、易于排序更新。

ex.q: Give one example of data stored in a food-delivery app's database.
ex.a: 1. Each dish's name, price, category, description (or each order's items, time and address).

ex.q: A student says 'a database is just any file with data in it, like a Word essay.' Correct?
ex.a:
1. No. A database stores structured data: records with the same fields.
  2. An essay is unstructured text.
ex.az: 1. 不对，数据库存放的是有结构的数据。

cards.en:
Intuition: the database is the filing cabinet; the DBMS is the librarian who builds it, files new papers and fetches what you ask for.

A DBMS is software used to create and manage databases.

Features:

  • create new databases; change the database schema (design)
  • insert and update records
  • retrieve data by searching (queries)
  • provide an interface for other programs to access the data
  • create forms for data input and reports to present data

Examples: Microsoft Access, MySQL, SQL Server.

Exam wording: "A DBMS is software that creates, maintains and controls access to a database."
cards.zh:
直觉：数据库是文件柜，DBMS 是管理员：建柜、存档、按要求取资料。

功能：建立数据库、修改结构（schema）、新增更新记录、搜寻检索、给其他程序接口、表单及报表。例子：Access、MySQL、SQL Server。

ex.q: Name TWO examples of DBMS.
ex.a:
1. Microsoft Access.
  2. MySQL (or SQL Server).

ex.q: A shop's website reads product prices from its database. Which DBMS feature makes this possible?
ex.a: 1. The DBMS provides an interface for other programs (the website) to access the data.

ex.q: A student writes 'Access is a database.' Improve the answer.
ex.a:
1. Access is a DBMS (software).
  2. The database is the collection of data (the .accdb file) it manages.
ex.az: 1. Access 是 DBMS；数据库是它管理的数据。

cards.en:
Intuition: the table is the store room. A form is the shop counter for adding one item at a time. A report is the printed stock list. A query is a question you ask the store room.

ObjectPurpose
TableStores data in records (rows) and fields (columns); the data source of the others
FormUser-friendly interface showing one record at a time for data entry
ReportDisplays and summarises data for printing
QueryFilters, sorts, summarises data; written in SQL

Create objects from the Create tab. Forms, reports and queries do not store data themselves.

Exam wording: "Only tables store data; forms, reports and queries use tables as their data source."
cards.zh:
直觉：Table 是仓库；Form 是一次处理一件货的柜台；Report 是印出来的存货单；Query 是向仓库提出的问题。

只有 Table 储存数据；其余三者以 table 为数据来源。

ex.q: Which object for: (a) clerks typing in new members; (b) printing a monthly summary; (c) finding members born after 2010?
ex.a:
1. (a) Form.
  2. (b) Report.
  3. (c) Query.

ex.q: A query result shows 20 records. Where are those records actually stored?
ex.a:
1. In the table the query reads from.
  2. The query only displays them.

ex.q: A student deletes a form and worries that all the member data is lost. Is it?
ex.a: 1. No. The data is in the table; the form was only an interface.

cards.en:
Intuition: datasheet view looks like Excel, but it is a strict form: you can only write inside the proper slots.

  • Each column is a field, each row is a record. There are no cell addresses.
  • You cannot type into any random cell; data must follow the table structure.
  • Last column "Click to Add": typing there adds a new field.
  • Last row marked *: typing there adds a new record.
  • (New) means the value (e.g. AutoNumber) is generated automatically.
  • You can delete the content of a field, a whole field (for all records) or a whole record, but you cannot delete a field for one record only.
  • Right-click a field name → Rename Field. Save/close the table, then right-click it in the object list to rename the object.
  • Unlike Excel, text formatting is shared by the whole table: one cell cannot have both black and blue text.
  • Finish input with Enter/Tab or by clicking another field; Esc undoes the input. Field names stay frozen at the top when scrolling.

Exam wording: "In datasheet view, each row is a record and each column is a field."
cards.zh:
直觉：Datasheet view 像 Excel，但很严格：只能在规定位置输入。

  • 每栏是 field，每行是 record；没有储存格位址。
  • "Click to Add" 加新 field；标 * 的行加新 record；(New) 表示自动产生（如 AutoNumber）。
  • 可以删除某栏位的内容、整个栏位（所有记录）或整条记录，但不能只删除一条记录的某个栏位。
  • 右键栏位名 → Rename Field 改名。
  • 与 Excel 不同，文字格式由整个 table 共用，不能一格黑字一格蓝字。
  • Enter/Tab 完成输入，Esc 取消输入。

ex.q: You need to add a new member. Where do you type in datasheet view?
ex.a: 1. In the last row marked *.

ex.q: In a STUDENT table with 6 students and 7 fields, how many records and fields?
ex.a:
1. Rows = records = 6.
  2. Columns = fields = 7.

ex.q: A student refers to 'cell B3' of an Access table in a report. What is wrong?
ex.a:
1. Access tables have no cell addresses.
  2. Refer to the field name and record, e.g. 'the CLASS of the record with SID S03'.
ex.az: 1. Access 没有储存格位址，要用 field 名称和 record。

cards.en:
Intuition: design view is the blueprint of the table. You see the plan of every field, not the data.

  • Shows no records; shows every field and lets you manage the table structure.
  • Each row is a field, with columns Field Name, Data Type, Description.
  • Field Properties panel: Field Size, Format, Decimal Places, Input Mask, Caption, Default Value, Validation Rule, Validation Text, Required, Indexed.
  • A key icon marks the primary key.
  • A field name can be up to 64 characters long, including spaces. Text formatting is not available in design view.
  • While a form, report or query using the table is open, you may not be allowed to change the table's data structure.

Exam wording: "Design view is used to define the structure of a table: field names, data types and field properties."
cards.zh:
直觉：Design view 是表格的蓝图：看到每个 field 的设计，不显示数据。

  • 每行是一个 field：Field Name、Data Type、Description。
  • Field Properties：Field Size、Format、Input Mask、Default Value、Validation Rule、Required 等。
  • 钥匙图示 = primary key。
  • 栏位名最长 64 个字符（包括空格）。Design view 不能设定文字格式。

ex.q: Marks must be from 0 to 100. Where and how do you enforce this?
ex.a:
1. Design view → select MARK → Field Properties.
  2. Validation Rule: Between 0 And 100.
  3. Validation Text: 'Mark must be 0–100'.

ex.q: New members should get SEX = 'F' unless changed. Which property?
ex.a: 1. Default Value = "F".

ex.q: A student opens design view to type in new records. What happens?
ex.a:
1. Design view shows no records; you cannot enter data there.
  2. Switch to datasheet view (or use a form).
ex.az: 1. Design view 不显示 record，要转到 datasheet view。

cards.en:
Intuition: a form is like a paper application form on screen: one person per page, with labelled boxes.

Forms let users manage data in a table using a user-friendly interface which shows one record at a time.

  • Create: select a table → Create → Form.
  • Form view: edit values, move with record navigation buttons, add a new blank record.
  • Layout view: change the layout.

Main purpose: simplify the user interface / facilitate data entry. It does not save storage or speed up calculations.

Exam wording: "A form provides a user-friendly interface for data entry, showing one record at a time."
cards.zh:
直觉：表单像屏幕上的申请表：一页一个人，有标签的输入框。

主要目的：简化用户界面、方便输入数据，一次显示一个 record。不会节省储存空间或加快运算。

ex.q: Why should office staff use a form instead of the table to enter new members?
ex.a:
1. A form shows one record at a time with clear labels.
  2. It is user-friendly and reduces input mistakes (e.g. typing in the wrong row).
ex.az: 1. 一次一个 record、界面友善，减少输入错误。

ex.q: Which view lets you rearrange the boxes on a form?
ex.a: 1. Layout view (or Design view).

ex.q: A student says 'a form saves storage space because it shows fewer fields'. Correct?
ex.a:
1. No. A form stores no data; the table still stores everything.
  2. Its purpose is to facilitate data entry.
ex.az: 1. 不对，表单不储存数据，目的是方便输入。

cards.en:
Intuition: a report is the neat printed summary you hand to the principal, not the messy store room.

Reports display and summarise data from tables in a customisable way for printing.

  • Create: select a table → Create → Report; edit in layout view.
  • Without changing table data you can: sort and filter, group records (Group On a field), remove fields, change format, add totals (Sum, Average, Count, Max, Min...).

Exam wording: "A report presents records in a specific order with summarised information (e.g. group totals) for printing."
cards.zh:
直觉：报表是交给校长的整齐打印摘要。

可排序、筛选、分组（Group On）、加总计（Sum、Average、Count...），不会改变 table 数据。

ex.q: Print a list of students grouped by class, with the average mark of each class.
ex.a:
1. Create a Report from STUDENT.
  2. Group On CLASS.
  3. Add a total on MARK → Average.
ex.az: 1. Report → Group On CLASS → MARK 加 Average。

ex.q: Give TWO common elements of a report.
ex.a:
1. Records in a specific order.
  2. Summarised information (totals, averages).

ex.q: A student uses a report to correct a wrong phone number. Possible?
ex.a:
1. No. Reports only display data.
  2. Edit the table (or use a form).

cards.en:
Intuition: a query is a question written in a special language (SQL) that the database understands: "show me all 5A students".

Queries filter, sort, summarise (update, delete) data in a table. They are written in Structured Query Language (SQL).

  1. Create → Query Design → close "Show Table".
  2. Switch to SQL view → type the statement.
  3. Click Run; the result appears in datasheet view.
  • A query result is a table, but nothing is stored; it is worked out each time.
  • Compare: a spreadsheet formula is stored in a cell and returns one value.

Exam wording: "A query returns data in the form of a table; running a SELECT query does not change the data."
cards.zh:
直觉：Query 是用数据库听得懂的语言（SQL）提出的问题。

  1. Create → Query Design → SQL view → 输入 → Run。

结果以表格形式显示，但不储存；SELECT 不会改变数据。

ex.q: Show every field of every record in STUDENT.
ex.a:
1. SELECT * FROM STUDENT.
  2. * means all fields.

ex.q: After running a SELECT query, does the STUDENT table change?
ex.a: 1. No. SELECT only retrieves data.

ex.q: A student says 'the query stores the answer in a new field of the table'. Correct?
ex.a:
1. Wrong. A query is not stored in any field.
  2. It returns a result table each time it is run.
ex.az: 1. 错，查询不储存在 field，每次执行才得出结果表。

code.src:
SELECT *
FROM STUDENT;

cards.tz: 数据库表结构 vs 试算表
cards.en:
Intuition: a spreadsheet is a free notebook page; a database table is a printed form with fixed boxes.

Database tableSpreadsheet
No empty columns or rowscan leave gaps anywhere
Each record has the same fieldsany cell can hold anything
Every value in a field shares the same properties (type, size, mask)each cell has its own format
Data type is defined before data entryformat is guessed after typing
No cell addressescell addresses (B4)

Exam wording: "A database table has a stricter structure: every record has the same fields and all data in a field share the same data type, so data are more consistent."
cards.zh:
直觉：试算表是自由的笔记页；数据库表是有固定格子的印刷表格。

  • 不能有空行空栏；每个 record 有相同 field；同一 field 所有值属性相同；数据类型在输入前定义；没有储存格位址。

ex.q: Give TWO differences between a database table and a spreadsheet.
ex.a:
1. Database: data type of each field is defined before entry; spreadsheet cells can hold any type.
  2. Database: no cell addresses; spreadsheet uses addresses like B4.
ex.az: 1. 数据类型预先定义；没有储存格位址。

ex.q: Why is the stricter structure useful?
ex.a:
1. It keeps data consistent (e.g. every DOB is a real date).
  2. This makes searching and sorting reliable.

ex.q: A student says 'in Access I can type a note in the MARK field of one student, like in Excel'. Correct?
ex.a: 1. No. If MARK is a Number field, every value must be a number; text is rejected.

cards.en:
Intuition: a data type tells the box what shape of thing it can hold: words, numbers, dates, yes/no.

TypeExampleNotes
TextHelloShort Text up to 255 characters
Number3.1416for calculation
Date/Time24/1/2015stored as a number, shown as a date
Currency$3.144 decimal places by default
AutoNumber1, 2, 3unique number generated automatically
Yes/No☑Boolean; true = −1, false = 0
  • Defined before data entry; changing it later may change stored values.
  • IDs/phones with leading zeros → Text.

Exam wording: "SID should be Text because a Number field does not store leading zeros."
cards.zh:
直觉：数据类型告诉格子能放哪种东西：文字、数字、日期、是/否。

Text（≤255 字）、Number、Date/Time（以数字储存）、Currency、AutoNumber（自动唯一编号）、Yes/No（Boolean）。有前导 0 的编号用 Text。

ex.q: Choose data types: member ID '000123', join date, fee paid ($), is_active.
ex.a:
1. ID → Text (keeps leading zeros).
  2. Join date → Date/Time.
  3. Fee → Currency.
  4. is_active → Yes/No.

ex.q: Which type automatically gives each new record a unique number?
ex.a: 1. AutoNumber.

ex.q: A student stores SID '034930' as Number. What is stored?
ex.a:
1. Number drops leading zeros → 34930.
  2. IDs that must look exact should be Text.

notes.t: Text ID keeps leading zeros; it is the primary key
notes.tz: 文字 ID 保留前导 0，为主键

code.out:
MID|JOINED|FEE|ACTIVE
000123|2026-09-01|350|1

cards.en:
Intuition: 124 = there are $124 in the piggy bank. 0 = the piggy bank is empty. NULL = there is no piggy bank at all.

  • A field with no data stored is NULL. NULL has no data type.
  • 0 is a Number value, not NULL. '' (empty text) is also not NULL in most DBMS.
  • Test with IS NULL / IS NOT NULL, never = NULL.
  • SUM, AVG, COUNT(field) ignore NULL; COUNT(*) counts all rows.
  • A primary key can never be NULL.

Exam wording: "NULL means no value is stored; it is different from 0, which is a number."
cards.zh:
直觉：124 = 钱罂有 $124；0 = 钱罂是空的；NULL = 根本没有钱罂。

  • NULL 表示没有储存数据，没有数据类型；0 是数字。
  • 用 IS NULL 测试，不可用 = NULL。
  • SUM、AVG、COUNT(field) 忽略 NULL；COUNT(*) 计所有行。

ex.q: In STUDENT, Ho Ka Lok's MARK is NULL. What is AVG(MARK)?
ex.a:
1. NULL is ignored: average of 78, 85, 62, 49, 91.
  2. Sum 365 / 5 = 73.

ex.q: Compare COUNT(*) and COUNT(MARK).
ex.a:
1. COUNT(*) counts rows → 6.
  2. COUNT(MARK) counts non-NULL marks → 5.

ex.q: A student writes WHERE MARK = NULL to find missing marks. Result?
ex.a:
1. Any comparison with NULL is unknown, so no rows are returned.
  2. Correct: WHERE MARK IS NULL.
ex.az: 1. 与 NULL 比较不会成立，结果为空；应用 IS NULL。

ex.q: A student says 'a mark of 0 is NULL'. Correct?
ex.a:
1. No. 0 is a stored number (the student scored zero).
  2. NULL means no mark was entered.

code.src:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS ROWS_,
 COUNT(MARK) AS MARKS,
 AVG(MARK) AS AVGMARK
FROM STUDENT;
code.out:
ROWS_|MARKS|AVGMARK
6|5|73.0

demo.query: SELECT CNAME, MARK FROM STUDENT WHERE MARK IS NULL;
demo.note: Only Ho Ka Lok has no mark stored. Try changing IS NULL to = NULL: no rows.

cards.en:
Intuition: a primary key is like an HKID number: no two people share it, and everyone must have one.

A primary key is a field that stores unique data for every record, used to identify a record from all others.

  • Values must be unique (no duplicates).
  • Values cannot be NULL.
  • Choose a field that should never have duplicates, not one that just happens to be unique now.
  • Set in design view: select field → Primary Key (key icon).

Exam wording: "SID is suitable as the primary key because each student has a unique student ID; CNAME is not, because two students may have the same name."
cards.zh:
直觉：像身份证号码：没有两人相同，而且人人都必须有。

  • 值必须唯一，且不能是 NULL。
  • 要选"永远不会重复"的 field，而不是"现在碰巧不重复"的。

ex.q: STUDENT(SID, CNAME, SEX, CLASS, DOB). Choose the primary key and explain.
ex.a:
1. SID: every student is given a unique ID and it is never empty.
  2. CNAME/DOB could repeat.

ex.q: In a BOOK table, which is better as primary key: ISBN or TITLE?
ex.a:
1. ISBN: unique for each edition.
  2. Different books can share a title.

ex.q: In the sample data all names are different, so a student picks CNAME as primary key. Comment.
ex.a:
1. Being unique now is not enough.
  2. A new student with the same name could not be added.
  3. Use SID.
ex.az: 1. 现在不重复不代表将来不会；应用 SID。

code.src:
INSERT INTO STUDENT(SID,CNAME)
VALUES('S01','New Kid');

notes.t: Try to add a record with SID
S01 already exists → rejected (UNIQUE constraint failed)
notes.tz: S01 已存在 → 被拒绝

code.out: Error: UNIQUE constraint failed: STUDENT.SID

cards.en:
Intuition: "Class 5A" is not unique and "number 12" is not unique, but "5A number 12" points to exactly one student.

A composite key is a primary key made of more than one field.

  • STUDENT: CLASS alone and CNO alone repeat, but CLASS + CNO is unique.
  • Sports day PARTICIPANT: EventID + StudentID (a student joins many events).
  • Order lines: OrderID + ItemID.
  • Set: select both fields in design view → Primary Key.

Exam wording: "CLASS and CNO together form a composite key since no two students have the same class and class number at the same time."
cards.zh:
直觉："5A" 不唯一，"12 号"不唯一，但"5A 12 号"只有一人。

Composite key：由多于一个 field 组成的主键。例子：CLASS+CNO、EventID+StudentID、OrderID+ItemID。

ex.q: PARTICIPANT(EventID, StudentID, Result). Suggest the primary key.
ex.a:
1. One student joins many events; one event has many students.
  2. Neither alone is unique; the pair is.
  3. Primary key = EventID + StudentID.

ex.q: LOAN(BookID, MemberID, LoanDate). A member may borrow the same book again later. Suggest a key.
ex.a:
1. BookID + MemberID could repeat on another day.
  2. Use BookID + MemberID + LoanDate (or add a LoanID).

ex.q: A student says CLASS is the primary key of STUDENT because every student has a class. Comment.
ex.a:
1. Every student has one, but it is not unique (30 students in 5A).
  2. Use CLASS + CNO (or SID).

notes.t: Composite primary key of two fields
notes.tz: 两个 field 组成复合主键

code.out: (table created)

cards.en:
Intuition: if nothing about a bus ticket is unique, the company prints a serial number on it.

Sometimes no field or combination can uniquely identify a record.

  • TRANSACTION(TDATE, TYPE, AMOUNT): two $20000 deposits on the same day are identical, so even all fields together can repeat.
  • Solution: add a new field (e.g. ID) giving each record a unique number, and make it the primary key.
  • Data type AutoNumber assigns it automatically.

Exam wording: "Add a field such as TID with AutoNumber data type as the primary key, since no existing field is unique."
cards.zh:
直觉：车票上没有独特资料时，就印上序号。

没有 field（或组合）能唯一识别 record 时：新增一个 ID field 作主键，类型用 AutoNumber 自动编号。

ex.q: TEMPERATURE(READ_TIME, PLACE, DEGREE) could have repeated readings. Suggest a primary key.
ex.a:
1. Add RID (AutoNumber).
  2. Each reading gets its own number.

ex.q: Why use AutoNumber for the new ID?
ex.a:
1. The DBMS generates a unique number for every new record automatically.
  2. Users cannot type a duplicate by mistake.
ex.az: 1. 自动产生唯一编号，不会人手重复。

ex.q: A student makes TDATE+TYPE+AMOUNT the composite key. Problem?
ex.a:
1. Two identical transactions on the same day would duplicate the key, so the second cannot be saved.
  2. Add an ID field instead.
ex.az: 1. 相同交易会令主键重复；应加 ID。

notes.t: Identical second deposit is still allowed
notes.tz: 相同的第二笔也可存入

cards.en:
Intuition: field size is the size of the box. Too small and things do not fit; too big wastes space and lets wrong data in.

  • The field size decides how much storage a field uses. A Text field of size N stores at most N characters.
  • A suitable size validates the data (length check) and saves storage space.
  • Number fields: size decides the range of numbers (Byte, Integer, Long Integer...).
FieldSizeReason
SID6always 6 characters
SEX1'M' or 'F'
CLASS2'5A'
CNAMElarge (e.g. 255)names vary in length

For some data types, like AutoNumber, the field size cannot be set (it is fixed or dynamic). A Number field holding a 2-digit number (0–99) needs fewer bits (7) than a Text field holding 2 characters (14), so it is usually smaller.

Exam wording: "Setting field size to 2 prevents input longer than 2 characters and saves storage space."
cards.zh:
直觉：field size 是盒子的大小：太小放不下，太大浪费空间又让错误数据进来。

  • Text field 大小 N = 最多 N 个字符；能做长度检查及节省空间。
  • Number field 的大小决定数值范围。

AutoNumber 等类型不能设定 field size。储存 0–99 的 Number 栏位只需 7 bits，比储存 2 个字符的 Text 栏位（14 bits）小。

ex.q: Suggest field sizes for HKID-style member code 'A1234567' and SEX.
ex.a:
1. Code is always 8 characters → size 8.
  2. SEX → size 1.

ex.q: Give TWO reasons to set CLASS to size 2.
ex.a:
1. Validation: '5AA' or ' 5A' (3 chars) is rejected.
  2. Saves storage space.

ex.q: A student sets CNAME (Chinese name) to size 3 since most names are 3 characters. Problem?
ex.a:
1. Some names have 4 characters or are English names.
  2. They cannot be stored. Use a larger size.
ex.az: 1. 有些名字较长会存不下；要设大一点。

cards.t: Minimum storage size and counting possible values
cards.tz: 最少储存空间与可能值的数量
cards.en:
Intuition: n bits give 2ⁿ different patterns. To store a value, find the smallest n with 2ⁿ ≥ number of possible values, then round up to whole bytes if asked.

  • 2-digit non-negative integer (0–99): 100 values → 7 bits (2⁷ = 128).
  • 2 ASCII characters in a Text field: each ≥ 7 bits → ≥ 14 bits. So a Number field is usually smaller than a Text field for the same digits.
  • Quantity up to 400,000: 2¹⁸ = 262,144 < 400,001 ≤ 2¹⁹ → 19 bits → 3 bytes.
  • A key of k bytes allows 2^(8k) different values, so at most that many unique records (2 bytes → 65,536).
  • Counting IDs: multiply the choices per position (digit 10, capital letter 26, binary flag 2).

Exam wording: "Minimum bits n satisfies 2ⁿ ≥ number of possible values; bytes = ⌈n ÷ 8⌉."
cards.zh:
直觉：n 个 bit 有 2ⁿ 种组合。找最小的 n 使 2ⁿ ≥ 可能值数目，需要时再进位成 byte。

  • 0–99：100 个值 → 7 bits。
  • 2 个 ASCII 字符 → 至少 14 bits，所以 Number 栏位通常比 Text 小。
  • 最多 400,000 → 19 bits → 3 bytes。
  • k bytes 的主键最多 2^(8k) 条唯一记录（2 bytes → 65,536）。
  • 计算编号数目：把每个位置的选择相乘。

ex.q: Minimum storage for a quantity field whose maximum is 400,000?
ex.a:
1. Values 0–400,000 → 400,001 values.
  2. 2¹⁸ = 262,144 too small; 2¹⁹ = 524,288 enough → 19 bits.
  3. 19 ÷ 8 → round up → 3 bytes.

ex.q: Book ID FGYYYYNNN: F = 0/1, G = A–Z, YYYY = year, NNN = 000–999. How many IDs for 2024?
A membership record's key field uses 2 bytes. How many unique records at most?
ex.a:
1. 2 bytes = 16 bits.
  2. 2¹⁶ = 65,536.

ex.q: A student says 0–99 needs 100 bits because there are 100 values. Correct?
ex.a:
1. No. Bits combine: 7 bits give 128 patterns.
  2. So 7 bits are enough.
ex.az: 1. 错。7 bits 已有 128 种组合，足够。

cards.en:
Intuition: an input mask is a stencil. Only the right kind of character fits in each hole.

An input mask ensures data is valid by restricting user input to a fixed pattern.

CharMeaning
0digit, required
9digit, optional
Lletter, required
?letter, optional
Aletter or digit, required
aletter or digit, optional
& / Cany character, required / optional
> / <following letters to UPPER / lower case
- / : .literal separators

More characters from the book's list: # = can be a digit, space, + or −; . decimal point; , thousands separator; : - / date and time separators; \ shows the next character literally; text in "double quotes" is shown literally. Book examples: phone 0000\-0000 → 3203-4930; student ID 000000 → 034930; class 0>L → 4A; month >L<LL → Jan. In a Number field the hyphen is only displayed, not stored.

Exam wording: "The input mask 0>L requires one digit followed by one letter, converted to uppercase."
cards.zh:
直觉：输入遮罩像模板：每个洞只放得进对的字符。

0 必须数字、9 可选数字、L 必须字母、? 可选字母、A 必须字母或数字、> 之后转大写、< 转小写。

其他字符：# 可为数字、空格、+ 或 −；. 小数点；, 千位分隔符；: - / 日期时间分隔符；\ 下一个字符照样显示；"..." 内文字照样显示。例：电话 0000\-0000、学生编号 000000、班别 0>L、月份 >L<LL。Number 栏位中的连字号只显示，不储存。

ex.q: CLASS like '5A' (digit then letter, always uppercase). Write the mask.
ex.a:
1. Digit required → 0.
  2. Make letters uppercase → >.
  3. Letter required → L.
  4. Mask: 0>L. Typing '5a' is stored as '5A'.

ex.q: HK phone shown as 2345-6789. Write the mask.
ex.a:
1. 8 required digits with a hyphen in the middle.
  2. 0000-0000.

ex.q: Does mask LL0000 accept 'AB123'?
ex.a:
1. Needs 2 letters + 4 digits.
  2. 'AB123' has only 3 digits → rejected.
ex.az: 1. 只有 3 个数字 → 不接受。

ex.q: A student uses mask 9999 for a 4-digit PIN that must be complete. Problem?
ex.a:
1. 9 means the digit is optional, so '12' would be accepted.
  2. Use 0000.
ex.az: 1. 9 是可选，会接受不足 4 位；应用 0000。

cards.en:
Intuition: the data type is what is inside the box; the format is the label printed on the outside.

  • Data type decides how a value is stored.
  • Format only decides how a value is displayed; it has no impact on the stored value.
  • Format looks like an input mask, but a mask controls input and a format controls display.

Example: 4 January 2015 shows as 4/1/2015 (General Date). An American may read it as 1 April. Format yyyy-mm-dd shows 2015-01-04; the stored date is the same.

Exam wording: "Format only changes how the data are displayed; the data type determines how data are stored."
cards.zh:
直觉：数据类型是盒子里的东西；format 是盒外的标签。

  • Data type 决定怎样储存；Format 只决定怎样显示。
  • Input mask 控制输入；Format 控制显示。

ex.q: DOB is shown as 4/1/2015 and confuses overseas staff. Fix without changing the data.
ex.a:
1. Set Format to yyyy-mm-dd.
  2. Displays 2015-01-04; the stored date is unchanged.

ex.q: Which controls what users can type: format or input mask?
ex.a:
1. Input mask.
  2. Format only affects display.

ex.q: A student sets the Format of a Text field to '>' and says the names are now stored in capitals. Correct?
ex.a:
1. No. They are only displayed in capitals.
  2. Stored values keep their original case.

cards.t: Database design: list and name the fields
cards.tz: 数据库设计：列出及命名 fields
cards.en:
Intuition: before building a cupboard you list what goes inside and label each drawer clearly.

Steps: 1. List the fields → 2. Name the fields → 3. Define the fields.

1. List the fields needed (e.g. student ID, Chinese name, English name, sex, class, class no., DOB, address, email). Pick one with no chance of duplication as primary key.

2. Name the fields: simple, meaningful, distinctive, with a consistent naming principle (CNAME, ENAME).

Avoid: spaces, underscores, special symbols, names of digits only, reserved words (SELECT, DATE, NAME...).

Exam wording: "Field names should be meaningful and should not contain spaces or reserved words, which may cause errors in some DBMS."
cards.zh:
直觉：造柜之前先列出要放什么，再清楚标示每个抽屉。

步骤：列出 → 命名 → 定义。命名要简单、有意义、易区分、一致；避免空格、底线、特殊符号、纯数字、保留字。

ex.q: List fields for a library MEMBER table.
ex.a: 1. MemberID (primary key), Name, Phone, Email, JoinDate, Active.

ex.q: Improve these names: 'Student Name', '1', 'date'.
ex.a:
1. 'Student Name' → SNAME (no space).
  2. '1' → a meaningful name, e.g. SCORE1.
  3. 'date' is a reserved word → DOB or JOINDATE.

ex.q: A student names fields Name, nm2, X. Comment.
ex.a:
1. Not consistent or meaningful: 'nm2' and 'X' tell nothing.
  2. Use e.g. CNAME, ENAME, CLASS.

cards.en:
Intuition: now decide the shape and size of each drawer.

3. Define: decide data type, field size, format, input mask for each field.

FieldTypeSizeFormat / Mask
SIDText6mask 000000
CNAME, ENAMEText255
SEXText1
CLASSText2mask 0>L
CNONumber
DOBDate/Timeformat yyyy-mm-dd
  • SID is Text: Number drops leading zeros.
  • CLASS size 2 + mask: rejects ' 5A' or '5a ' which would break sorting/filtering.

Exam wording: "Each field's data type and properties are chosen according to the data to be stored, to validate input and save space."
cards.zh:
直觉：决定每个抽屉的形状和大小。

为每个 field 定数据类型、大小、format、input mask。SID 用 Text（保留前导 0）；CLASS 大小 2 + 0>L，避免 ' 5A' 之类影响排序筛选。

ex.q: Define CNO (class number 1–40).
ex.a:
1. Number type (used for sorting numerically).
  2. Validation Rule Between 1 And 40.

ex.q: Define EMAIL.
ex.a:
1. Text, size large enough (e.g. 255).
  2. Validation rule: Like "*@*.*".

ex.q: A student makes CNO a Text field. Sorting gives 1, 10, 11, 2, 3... Why?
ex.a:
1. Text is sorted character by character, so '10' comes before '2'.
  2. Use a Number field.
ex.az: 1. 文字逐字比较，'10' 排在 '2' 前；应用 Number。

code.src:
CREATE TABLE STUDENT2(
 SID TEXT(6) PRIMARY KEY,
 CNAME TEXT(255),
 SEX TEXT(1),
 CLASS TEXT(2),
 CNO INTEGER CHECK (CNO BETWEEN 1 AND 40),
 DOB DATE);

notes.t: Number with a range check (validation rule)

code.out: (table created)

cards.en:
Intuition: pick the smallest box that always fits, and the box that blocks wrong things.

DataChoiceWhy
8-digit HK phoneNumber (or Text)Number saves space: 99,999,999 fits in 27 bits, 8 characters need ≥56 bits; hyphen shown by mask
Phone with +852, spaces, leading 0Textsymbols and leading zeros
REGISTERED yes/noYes/Noless storage, and only TRUE/FALSE possible (no 'NONE')
Registration dateDate/Timestore the date, not "days since"; it never needs updating

Exam wording: "Yes/No data type takes less storage space and only allows two values, so invalid data cannot be entered."
cards.zh:
直觉：选一个永远放得下、又能挡住错误的最小盒子。

  • 8 位电话：Number 较省空间；有 +852 或前导 0 → Text。
  • 是否登记：Yes/No，较省空间又只容许两个值。
  • 登记日期用 Date/Time，而不是"已过天数"（要天天更新）。

ex.q: Explain why 8-digit phone numbers stored as Number use less space than Text.
ex.a:
1. Text: 8 characters × at least 7 bits = ≥56 bits.
  2. Number: 99,999,999 < 227 (134,217,728), so 27 bits are enough.

ex.q: A field DAYS_SINCE_JOIN is stored for each member. Suggest a better design.
ex.a:
1. Store JOINDATE (Date/Time).
  2. Days since can be calculated when needed; a stored count becomes wrong every day.

ex.q: REGISTERED is stored as Text 'YES'/'NO'. A student says this is just as good as Yes/No. Comment.
ex.a:
1. Text allows wrong values like 'Y', 'yes ', 'NONE' (unless masked) and uses more storage.
  2. Yes/No only allows TRUE/FALSE and is smaller.
ex.az: 1. Text 可输入错误值且较占空间；应用 Yes/No。

cards.en:
Intuition: same as Excel filters: hide what you do not need, delete nothing.

  • Types: text filter, number filter, date filter.
  • Click the arrow on a field name → tick/untick values, or e.g. Date Filters → Between…
  • More than one filter can be applied (combined with AND).
  • Toggle Filter: removes the filter temporarily; click again to restore it.
  • Advanced → Clear All Filters: removes filters permanently.

In SQL, filtering = WHERE.

Exam wording: "Filtering displays only records that meet the criteria without deleting any record."
cards.zh:
直觉：同 Excel：隐藏不需要的，不删除任何东西。

  • Text/Number/Date filter；可同时用多个（以 AND 组合）。
  • Toggle Filter 暂时取消，再按恢复；Clear All Filters 永久清除。
  • SQL 对应 WHERE。

ex.q: Show only female students in 5C.
ex.a:
1. Filter SEX → tick F only.
  2. Filter CLASS → tick 5C only.
  3. Both filters apply together (AND) → Amy Cheung.

ex.q: Show students born between 1 Jan and 30 Jun 2010.
ex.a:
1. DOB arrow → Date Filters → Between… 2010-01-01 and 2010-06-30.
  2. Result: Chan Tai Man, Wong Siu Fan, Tom Ho.
ex.az: 1. Between… → Chan Tai Man、Wong Siu Fan、Tom Ho。

ex.q: A student clicks Toggle Filter and thinks the filter is gone forever. Correct?
ex.a:
1. No. Toggle Filter only removes it temporarily.
  2. Use Clear All Filters to remove it permanently.
ex.az: 1. 只是暂时取消；永久清除用 Clear All Filters。

demo.query:
SELECT CNAME, DOB FROM STUDENT
WHERE DOB BETWEEN '2010-01-01' AND '2010-06-30';
demo.note: A date filter 'Between…' does the same as this WHERE clause.

cards.en:
Intuition: line up the records by height, by name, by date...

  • By default, records are sorted by the primary key in ascending order.
  • Ascending = A→Z / smallest→largest / oldest→newest; Descending = the reverse.
  • Multiple criteria: sort one field, then another.
  • Remove Sort clears all sorting and returns to the default (primary key ascending).

In SQL, sorting = ORDER BY.

Exam wording: "Records are sorted by the primary key in ascending order by default."
cards.zh:
直觉：按高度、名字、日期把记录排好。

  • 预设按主键升序。
  • Remove Sort 清除所有排序，回到预设。
  • SQL 对应 ORDER BY。

ex.q: Show the tallest students first.
ex.a:
1. HEIGHT arrow → Sort Largest to Smallest (descending).
  2. Tom Ho (180) appears first.

ex.q: After many sorts, how do you get back the original order?
ex.a: 1. Remove Sort → back to primary key (SID) ascending.

ex.q: A student says 'Remove Sort puts records back in the order I typed them'. Correct?
ex.a: 1. Not exactly: it returns to primary key ascending, which may differ from typing order.
ex.az: 1. 是回到主键升序，不一定是输入次序。

demo.query: SELECT CNAME, HEIGHT FROM STUDENT ORDER BY HEIGHT DESC;
demo.note: Sort Largest to Smallest on HEIGHT = ORDER BY HEIGHT DESC.

cards.en:
Intuition: SELECT = "which columns do I want to see?"; FROM = "from which table?".

SELECT field1, field2
FROM table
  • SELECT lists the fields/expressions to show, in the order you want.
  • FROM gives the table name.
  • * means all fields.
  • The result is a temporary table; the source table is not changed.

Exam wording: "SELECT CNAME, CLASS FROM STUDENT displays the CNAME and CLASS of all records in STUDENT."
cards.zh:
直觉：SELECT = 要看哪些栏；FROM = 来自哪个表。

  • * = 所有 field；栏的次序可自由排列。
  • 结果是临时表，原表不变。

ex.q: Show the class and name of every student, class first.
ex.a:
1. Fields in the order wanted: CLASS, CNAME.
  2. SELECT CLASS, CNAME FROM STUDENT.
  3. 6 rows, 2 columns.

ex.q: How many rows and columns does SELECT * FROM STUDENT return?
ex.a:
1. All 6 records.
  2. All 7 fields.
  3. 6 rows × 7 columns.

ex.q: A student writes SELECT CNAME, CLASS STUDENT. Error?
ex.a:
1. The keyword FROM is missing.
  2. Correct: SELECT CNAME, CLASS FROM STUDENT.

code.src:
SELECT CLASS, CNAME
FROM STUDENT;

notes.t: Choose two fields, CLASS shown first
notes.tz: 选两个 field，CLASS 先显示

code.out:
CLASS|CNAME
5A|Chan Tai Man
5A|Lee Mei Ling
5B|Ho Ka Lok
5B|Wong Siu Fan
5C|Tom Ho
5C|Amy Cheung

demo.query: SELECT CLASS, CNAME FROM STUDENT;
demo.note: Change the field list and press Run to see different columns.

cards.en:
Intuition: a formula lives in one cell and gives one value; a query is a question you ask the database and it gives back a whole table.

Formula (spreadsheet)Query (database)
Stored wherein a cell of a worksheetnot stored in any field of a table (it is its own Access object)
Returnsa value after evaluationdata in the form of a table after execution
Changes source data?-a SELECT query never changes the table; calculated columns appear in the result only
Summarise groupspivot tableGROUP BY

Exam wording: "A query returns a table of records and does not alter the source table."
cards.zh:
直觉：公式住在一个储存格，给一个值；查询是向数据库提问，给回一整个表。

  • 公式储存在 worksheet 的储存格，计算后传回一个值。
  • Query 不储存在任何栏位，执行后传回一个表。
  • SELECT 不会改变原本的 table。
  • 试算表用 pivot table 汇总；数据库用 GROUP BY。

ex.q: Where is =AVERAGE(D2:F2) stored, and what does it return?
ex.a:
1. In one cell (e.g. G2).
  2. It returns one value, the mean of D2:F2.
ex.az: 1. 储存在一个储存格，传回一个值。

ex.q: SELECT CNAME, (SCORE1+SCORE2)/2 FROM STUDENT. Is a new field added to STUDENT?
ex.a:
1. The expression appears as a column (e.g. Expr1000) in the result.
  2. No field is added; the table is unchanged.
ex.az: 1. 只在结果显示，不会新增栏位。

ex.q: A spreadsheet uses a pivot table to total profit per team. What is the SQL equivalent idea?
ex.a:
1. Group the records by team.
  2. SELECT MANAGEDBY, SUM(PROFIT) FROM SALES GROUP BY MANAGEDBY.

ex.q: A student says running SELECT UCASE(ENAME) FROM STUDENT turns all names in the table into capitals. Right?
ex.a:
1. SELECT only shows a result.
  2. The values stored in ENAME remain unchanged.
ex.az: 1. SELECT 只显示结果，ENAME 的值不变。

cards.tz: 计算、AS 与算术运算符
cards.en:
Intuition: you can ask the database to do sums on each row, and give the new column a nice name tag (AS).

  • Expressions in SELECT: SELECT CNAME, MARK + 5 FROM STUDENT.
  • The new column appears only in the result; no field is added to the table.
  • AS gives an alias (column name): MARK * 1.1 AS NEWMARK. Optional, but improves readability.
  • Operators: + − * /, normal order of operations; use ( ) only.
  • In Access, + also joins text: CNAME + ' ' + ENAME (other DBMS use || or CONCAT).

Exam wording: "The calculated column is shown in the query result only; the table is not changed."
cards.zh:
直觉：可以叫数据库逐行计算，并用 AS 给新栏一个名字。

  • 计算栏只在结果中出现，不会加到表。
  • AS = 别名（可省略）。运算符 + − * /，括号只用 ( )。
  • Access 中 + 也可连接文字。

ex.q: Show each name and mark scaled up by 10% as NEWMARK.
ex.a:
1. SELECT CNAME, MARK * 1.1 AS NEWMARK FROM STUDENT.
  2. Chan Tai Man: 78 × 1.1 = 85.8.

ex.q: Height is in cm. Show it in metres as H_M.
ex.a:
1. SELECT CNAME, HEIGHT / 100.0 AS H_M FROM STUDENT.
  2. 172 → 1.72.

ex.q: A student writes SELECT (MARK + 10) / 2 AS HALF FROM STUDENT and expects Ho Ka Lok to get 5. Result?
ex.a:
1. Ho Ka Lok's MARK is NULL.
  2. Any arithmetic with NULL gives NULL, not 5.
ex.az: 1. NULL 参与运算结果仍是 NULL。

ex.q: A student writes SELECT MARK + 5 / 2 FROM STUDENT to get (mark+5)/2. Result for 78?
ex.a:
1. / is done first: 5/2 = 2.5 → 78 + 2.5 = 80.5, not 41.5.
  2. Correct: (MARK + 5) / 2.0.

code.src:
SELECT CNAME,
 ROUND(MARK * 1.1, 1) AS NEWMARK,
 HEIGHT / 100.0 AS H_M
FROM STUDENT;

notes.t: Mark × 1.1 rounded to 1 d.p., named NEWMARK
notes.tz: 分数 × 1.1（1 位小数），命名 NEWMARK

code.out:
CNAME|NEWMARK|H_M
Chan Tai Man|85.8|1.72
Lee Mei Ling|93.5|1.6
Ho Ka Lok|NULL|1.68
Wong Siu Fan|68.2|1.55
Tom Ho|53.9|1.8
Amy Cheung|100.1|1.63

demo.query: SELECT CNAME, MARK, (MARK + 10) / 2.0 AS HALF FROM STUDENT;
demo.note: Notice Ho Ka Lok: NULL in, NULL out.

cards.en:
Intuition: WHERE is a gate: only rows that pass the test come through. DISTINCT removes repeated rows from the answer.

SELECT CNAME, DOB FROM STUDENT
WHERE SEX = 'M' AND DOB < #2010-04-01#
  • Text in single quotes: 'M'.
  • Numbers: no quotes: MARK > 60.
  • Dates: in Access between #: #2010-04-01#; other DBMS use '2010-04-01'.
  • DISTINCT filters out duplicate rows: SELECT DISTINCT CLASS FROM STUDENT.

Exam wording: "DISTINCT is used to remove duplicate values so each class is listed once."
cards.zh:
直觉：WHERE 是闸门，只有通过测试的行才出现；DISTINCT 去除重复。

  • 文字用单引号；数字不加引号；Access 日期用 #…#（其他 DBMS 用 '…'）。
  • DISTINCT：每个值只列一次。

ex.q: List names of all girls.
ex.a:
1. Text value → quotes.
  2. SELECT CNAME FROM STUDENT WHERE SEX = 'F'.
  3. Lee Mei Ling, Wong Siu Fan, Amy Cheung.

ex.q: List each class once.
ex.a:
1. SELECT DISTINCT CLASS FROM STUDENT.
  2. Result: 5A, 5B, 5C (3 rows, not 6).

ex.q: In Access, list boys born before 1 April 2010.
ex.a:
1. SELECT CNAME FROM STUDENT WHERE SEX = 'M' AND DOB < #2010-04-01#.
  2. Chan Tai Man (2010-03-12), Ho Ka Lok (2009-11-02).

ex.q: A student writes WHERE SEX = F. What goes wrong?
ex.a:
1. Without quotes, F is read as a field name, which does not exist → error (Access asks for a parameter).
  2. Correct: SEX = 'F'.
ex.az: 1. 没有引号，F 被当作 field 名称；应写 'F'。

notes.t: Only boys born before 1 Apr 2010 (in Access: #2010-04-01#)
notes.tz: 只要 2010-04-01 前出生的男生（Access 用 #…#）

code.out:
CNAME|DOB
Chan Tai Man|2010-03-12
Ho Ka Lok|2009-11-02

code.src:
SELECT DISTINCT CLASS
FROM STUDENT;
code.out:
CLASS
5A
5B
5C

demo.query: SELECT DISTINCT CLASS FROM STUDENT;
demo.note: Remove DISTINCT and run again: 6 rows with repeats.

cards.t: Comparison operators and data type mismatch
cards.tz: 比较运算符与类型不符
cards.en:
Intuition: compare like with like. Asking "is the word '35' bigger than the number 35?" makes no sense to the database.

OperatorMeaning
=equal
<>not equal
< > <= >=less/greater (or equal)
  • Text is compared in dictionary order: 'cat' < 'dog', 'apple' < 'application'. In most DBMS text comparison is case sensitive.
  • Data types must match, else "Data type mismatch in criteria expression". SID is Text → SID > 'S03', not SID > 3.

Exam wording: "Since SID is a Text field, the value must be enclosed in quotation marks."
cards.zh:
直觉：同类才能比较。

  • = <> < > <= >=。
  • 文字按字典次序比较，多数 DBMS 分大小写。
  • 类型要一致，否则 "Data type mismatch"；SID 是 Text 要加引号。

ex.q: List students with MARK of at least 60.
ex.a:
1. SELECT CNAME, MARK FROM STUDENT WHERE MARK >= 60.
  2. Chan Tai Man 78, Lee Mei Ling 85, Wong Siu Fan 62, Amy Cheung 91.

ex.q: List students not in 5A.
ex.a:
1. WHERE CLASS <> '5A'.
  2. 4 students (5B and 5C).

ex.q: Is 'apple' < 'application' TRUE?
ex.a:
1. Compare letter by letter: a-p-p-l are equal.
  2. Next: 'e' vs 'i': e comes first → TRUE.
ex.az: 1. 逐字比较，e 在 i 前 → TRUE。

ex.q: A student writes WHERE SID > 3 in Access (SID is Text). Result?
ex.a:
1. Text field compared with a number → Data type mismatch in criteria expression.
  2. Correct: WHERE SID > 'S03'.

notes.t: Text compared with text in quotes → S04, S05, S06
notes.tz: 文字与带引号文字比较

code.out:
SID|CNAME
S04|Wong Siu Fan
S05|Tom Ho
S06|Amy Cheung

demo.query: SELECT CNAME, MARK FROM STUDENT WHERE MARK >= 60;
demo.note: Ho Ka Lok (NULL) is never returned by a comparison.

cards.en:
Intuition: AND narrows the search (both must be true); OR widens it (either one is enough); NOT flips it.

OperatorTRUE when
ANDall conditions are TRUE
ORat least one is TRUE
NOTthe condition is FALSE
  • Range 20–25: AGE >= 20 AND AGE <= 25. With OR it is always true.
  • NOT AGE < 25 = AGE >= 25.
  • AND is evaluated before OR: use parentheses when mixing.

Exam wording: "Parentheses are needed because AND has a higher precedence than OR."
cards.zh:
直觉：AND 收窄（全部要真）；OR 放宽（一个真就可）；NOT 反转。

  • 范围要用 AND；用 OR 会永远成立。
  • AND 先于 OR，混用时加括号。

ex.q: Girls with MARK above 80.
ex.a:
1. WHERE SEX = 'F' AND MARK > 80.
  2. Lee Mei Ling (85), Amy Cheung (91).

ex.q: Students in 5A or 5C who are taller than 170.
ex.a:
1. Group the OR in brackets: WHERE (CLASS = '5A' OR CLASS = '5C') AND HEIGHT > 170.
  2. Chan Tai Man (172), Tom Ho (180).
ex.az: 1. 括号包住 OR → Chan Tai Man、Tom Ho。

ex.q: A student writes WHERE CLASS = '5A' OR CLASS = '5C' AND HEIGHT > 170. What is returned?
ex.a:
1. AND first: (CLASS='5C' AND HEIGHT>170) → Tom Ho.
  2. OR CLASS='5A' adds all 5A: Chan Tai Man, Lee Mei Ling (160!).
  3. Lee Mei Ling is wrongly included. Add parentheses.
ex.az: 1. AND 先算，结果多了 Lee Mei Ling；要加括号。

code.src:
SELECT CNAME, CLASS, HEIGHT
FROM STUDENT
WHERE (CLASS = '5A' OR CLASS = '5C')
 AND HEIGHT > 170;

notes.t: Class is 5A or 5C (brackets make OR go first)
notes.tz: 5A 或 5C（括号令 OR 先算）

code.out:
CNAME|CLASS|HEIGHT
Chan Tai Man|5A|172
Tom Ho|5C|180

demo.query:
SELECT CNAME, CLASS, HEIGHT FROM STUDENT
WHERE CLASS = '5A' OR CLASS = '5C' AND HEIGHT > 170;
demo.note: No brackets: AND runs first, so every 5A student appears. Add brackets and compare.

cards.en:
Intuition: IN is a guest list ("only these names"); BETWEEN is a height bar ("from here to there, both ends included").

  • IN lists several values: CLASS IN ('5A','5C') = CLASS='5A' OR CLASS='5C'.
  • BETWEEN a AND b is inclusive: MARK BETWEEN 60 AND 85 = MARK >= 60 AND MARK <= 85.
  • Works for numbers, text and dates (Access dates: #…#).

Exam wording: "BETWEEN … AND is inclusive: both boundary values are included."
cards.zh:
直觉：IN 是宾客名单；BETWEEN 是由某处到某处（包括两端）。

  • IN (…) = 多个 OR。
  • BETWEEN a AND b = >= a AND <= b。

ex.q: Students in 5A or 5C, using IN.
ex.a:
1. WHERE CLASS IN ('5A','5C').
  2. Chan Tai Man, Lee Mei Ling, Tom Ho, Amy Cheung.

ex.q: Marks from 62 to 85 inclusive.
ex.a:
1. WHERE MARK BETWEEN 62 AND 85.
  2. 78, 85, 62 → Chan Tai Man, Lee Mei Ling, Wong Siu Fan (62 and 85 included).

ex.q: A student writes WHERE MARK > 62 AND MARK < 85 as the same as BETWEEN 62 AND 85. Difference?
ex.a:
1. > and < exclude the ends: only 78 is returned.
  2. BETWEEN includes 62 and 85. Use >= and <=.

code.out:
CNAME|MARK
Chan Tai Man|78
Lee Mei Ling|85
Wong Siu Fan|62

notes.t: Class is any value in the list

code.out:
CNAME|CLASS
Chan Tai Man|5A
Lee Mei Ling|5A
Tom Ho|5C
Amy Cheung|5C

demo.query: SELECT CNAME, MARK FROM STUDENT WHERE MARK BETWEEN 62 AND 85;
demo.note: Both 62 and 85 are included.

cards.en:
Intuition: wildcards are jokers in a card game: they can stand for any letter.

MeaningAccessOthers (MySQL, SQLite)
any number of characters (0 or more)*%
exactly one character?_
  • LIKE 'Ho*' starts with Ho; '*Ho' ends with Ho; '*Ho*' contains Ho; '??' exactly 2 characters.
  • First check which syntax (Access or other) the question uses.

Exam wording: "LIKE '%ing' selects values ending with 'ing'; % represents any number of characters."
cards.zh:
直觉：通配符像啤牌中的鬼牌，可代替任何字。

  • Access：* 任意多个、? 一个；其他 DBMS：% 和 _。
  • 先看题目用哪种语法。

ex.q: (SQLite) Names starting with 'Ho'.
ex.a:
1. WHERE CNAME LIKE 'Ho%'.
  2. Ho Ka Lok.

ex.q: (SQLite) Names containing 'Ho' anywhere.
ex.a:
1. WHERE CNAME LIKE '%Ho%'.
  2. Ho Ka Lok, Tom Ho.

ex.q: (Access) Classes with exactly 2 characters starting with 5.
ex.a:
1. WHERE CLASS LIKE '5?'.
  2. 5A, 5B, 5C all match.

ex.q: A student in MySQL writes WHERE CNAME LIKE 'Ho*'. Result?
ex.a:
1. In MySQL, * is a normal character, not a wildcard.
  2. No name literally 'Ho*' → no rows. Use 'Ho%'.
ex.az: 1. MySQL 中 * 不是通配符，结果为空；应用 %。

code.out:
CNAME
Ho Ka Lok
Tom Ho

demo.query: SELECT CNAME FROM STUDENT WHERE CNAME LIKE '%Ho%';
demo.note: Try 'Ho%' (starts with) or '%Ho' (ends with).

cards.t: IS NULL and IS NOT NULL
cards.tz: IS NULL 与 IS NOT NULL
cards.en:
Intuition: NULL is "nothing there", so you cannot ask "is it equal to nothing?". You ask "IS it empty?".

  • Use IS NULL / IS NOT NULL, never = NULL.
  • A primary key can never be NULL, so WHERE SID IS NOT NULL filters out nothing.

Exam wording: "WHERE MARK IS NULL selects records with no value stored in MARK."
cards.zh:
直觉：NULL 是"什么都没有"，不能问"是否等于没有"，要问"是不是空"。

  • 用 IS NULL / IS NOT NULL，不可用 = NULL。
  • 主键不会是 NULL，WHERE 主键 IS NOT NULL 不会筛走任何记录。

ex.q: Find students whose mark is missing.
ex.a:
1. SELECT CNAME FROM STUDENT WHERE MARK IS NULL.
  2. Ho Ka Lok.

ex.q: How many rows does SELECT * FROM STUDENT WHERE SID IS NOT NULL return?
ex.a:
1. SID is the primary key, never NULL.
  2. All 6 rows.

ex.q: A student writes WHERE MARK <> NULL to list students with marks. Result?
ex.a:
1. Comparisons with NULL are never TRUE → 0 rows.
  2. Correct: WHERE MARK IS NOT NULL (5 rows).

notes.t: Only records where a mark is stored

code.out:
CNAME|MARK
Chan Tai Man|78
Lee Mei Ling|85
Wong Siu Fan|62
Tom Ho|49
Amy Cheung|91

demo.query: SELECT CNAME FROM STUDENT WHERE MARK <> NULL;
demo.note: Returns nothing! Change to WHERE MARK IS NOT NULL.

cards.en:
Intuition: ORDER BY lines up the answer, like sorting a class list by marks.

  • ASC = ascending (default, can be omitted); DESC = descending.
  • Several keys: ORDER BY CLASS ASC, MARK DESC. Later keys only break ties.
  • Clause order: SELECT … FROM … WHERE … GROUP BY … HAVING … ORDER BY (always last).

Exam wording: "Records are sorted by CLASS in ascending order, and records with the same CLASS by MARK in descending order."
cards.zh:
直觉：ORDER BY 把结果排好，像按分数排名单。

  • ASC 升序（预设）、DESC 降序。
  • 多个准则：后面的只在前面相同时才起作用。
  • 子句次序：SELECT、FROM、WHERE、GROUP BY、HAVING、ORDER BY（最后）。

ex.q: List names and marks from highest to lowest mark.
ex.a:
1. SELECT CNAME, MARK FROM STUDENT ORDER BY MARK DESC.
  2. Amy Cheung 91 first. (In SQLite NULL comes last when DESC.)

ex.q: Sort by CLASS, then tallest first within each class.
ex.a:
1. ORDER BY CLASS, HEIGHT DESC.
  2. 5A: Chan Tai Man (172), Lee Mei Ling (160); 5B: Ho Ka Lok, Wong Siu Fan; 5C: Tom Ho, Amy Cheung.

ex.q: A student writes SELECT CNAME FROM STUDENT ORDER BY MARK WHERE SEX = 'F'. Error?
ex.a:
1. Clause order is wrong: WHERE must come before ORDER BY.
  2. Correct: ... WHERE SEX = 'F' ORDER BY MARK.
ex.az: 1. WHERE 要在 ORDER BY 之前。

notes.t: Sort by class A→Z; same class → taller first
notes.tz: 先按班别，同班再按身高降序

code.out:
CLASS|CNAME|HEIGHT
5A|Chan Tai Man|172
5A|Lee Mei Ling|160
5B|Ho Ka Lok|168
5B|Wong Siu Fan|155
5C|Tom Ho|180
5C|Amy Cheung|163

demo.query: SELECT CLASS, CNAME, HEIGHT FROM STUDENT ORDER BY CLASS ASC, HEIGHT DESC;
demo.note: Within each class, the taller student is listed first.

cards.tz: 数学函数 INT 与 ABS
cards.en:
Intuition: same as Excel: INT chops down to a whole number; ABS removes the minus sign.

  • INT(number): rounds down to the nearest integer; negatives go away from 0: INT(−2.3) = −3.
  • ABS(number): absolute value: ABS(−10) = 10.
  • A SELECT never changes stored data: CREDIT is the same after the query.
  • (INT is Access; in SQLite use CAST(x AS INTEGER) for positives, which truncates toward 0.)

Exam wording: "INT() rounds down the value; the stored data are not changed by the SELECT statement."
cards.zh: 直觉：同 Excel：INT 向下取整（负数离 0），ABS 去负号。SELECT 不会改变储存的数据。

ex.q: CREDIT = 154.60. What does SELECT INT(CREDIT) show (Access)?
ex.a: 1. Round down → 154 ($154.00 if the field is Currency).

ex.q: Show how far each mark is from 70.
ex.a:
1. SELECT CNAME, ABS(MARK - 70) AS GAP FROM STUDENT.
  2. Tom Ho: |49 − 70| = 21.

ex.q: A student expects INT(-2.3) to be −2. Correct?
ex.a: 1. No. INT rounds down, so −2.3 → −3.

notes.t: Distance of mark from 70, always positive

code.out:
CNAME|GAP
Chan Tai Man|8
Lee Mei Ling|15
Ho Ka Lok|NULL
Wong Siu Fan|8
Tom Ho|21
Amy Cheung|21

demo.query: SELECT CNAME, MARK, ABS(MARK - 70) AS GAP FROM STUDENT;
demo.note: ABS removes the minus sign for marks below 70.

cards.tz: 文字函数 LEN 与 MID
cards.en:
Intuition: LEN measures a string like a ruler; MID cuts a slice from the middle.

  • LEN(text): number of characters; a space counts. (Others: LENGTH, CHAR_LENGTH.)
  • MID(text, start, n): n characters from position start (counting from 1). (Others: SUBSTR, SUBSTRING.)

Exam wording: "LEN('Chan Tai Man') returns 12 because spaces are counted."
cards.zh: 直觉：LEN 是尺，量字符数（空格也算）；MID 从中间切一片：MID(文字, 开始位置, 个数)，位置由 1 起。其他 DBMS：LENGTH、SUBSTR。

ex.q: Evaluate LEN('Chan Tai Man').
Get the class level digit from CLASS '5A'.
ex.a:
1. Access: MID(CLASS, 1, 1) → '5'.
  2. SQLite: SUBSTR(CLASS, 1, 1).

ex.q: A student uses MID(SID, 0, 2) to get the first 2 characters. Problem?
ex.a:
1. Positions start at 1, not 0.
  2. Use MID(SID, 1, 2) → 'S0'.

code.src:
SELECT CNAME,
 LENGTH(CNAME) AS LEN_,
 SUBSTR(CNAME, 1, 3) AS FIRST3
FROM STUDENT;

notes.tz: 前 3 个字符（Access 用 MID）

code.out:
CNAME|LEN_|FIRST3
Chan Tai Man|12|Cha
Lee Mei Ling|12|Lee
Ho Ka Lok|9|Ho 
Wong Siu Fan|12|Won
Tom Ho|6|Tom
Amy Cheung|10|Amy

demo.query: SELECT CNAME, LENGTH(CNAME) AS LEN_, SUBSTR(CNAME, 6, 3) AS PART FROM STUDENT;
demo.note: LENGTH/SUBSTR are the SQLite names for LEN/MID.

cards.en:
Intuition: tidy-up tools for text: change case, cut extra spaces, or add spaces.

AccessOthersMeaning
LCASE / UCASELOWER / UPPERto lower / upper case
TRIMTRIMremove spaces at the beginning and end (not the middle)
SPACE(n)(none in SQLite)a string of n spaces

The stored values remain unchanged.

Exam wording: "TRIM removes leading and trailing spaces only."
cards.zh: 直觉：整理文字的工具：转大小写、去头尾空格、加空格。Access 用 LCASE/UCASE，其他 DBMS 用 LOWER/UPPER；TRIM 只去头尾空格；SPACE(n) 产生 n 个空格。储存值不变。

ex.q: Show all names in capitals (Access and SQLite).
ex.a:
1. Access: SELECT UCASE(CNAME) FROM STUDENT.
  2. SQLite: SELECT UPPER(CNAME) FROM STUDENT.

ex.q: Evaluate TRIM('  When a tree falls  ').
ex.a:
1. Spaces at both ends removed; middle spaces kept.
  2. → 'When a tree falls'.

ex.q: A student uses TRIM to turn 'Tom    Ho' into 'Tom Ho' in Access SQL. Works?
ex.a:
1. No. SQL TRIM only removes leading and trailing spaces; the middle stays.
  2. (Excel's TRIM does reduce middle spaces; SQL's does not.)
ex.az: 1. SQL 的 TRIM 只去头尾，中间空格不变（与 Excel 不同）。

code.src:
SELECT UPPER(CNAME) AS BIG,
 LOWER(CNAME) AS SMALL,
 '[' || TRIM('  Tom Ho  ') || ']' AS T
FROM STUDENT WHERE SID = 'S05';

notes.t: TRIM removes end spaces; [ ] show the edges (|| joins text in SQLite)
notes.tz: TRIM 去头尾空格；|| 在 SQLite 连接文字

code.out:
BIG|SMALL|T
TOM HO|tom ho|[Tom Ho]

cards.t: GROUP BY with MAX and MIN
cards.en:
Intuition: GROUP BY sorts students into piles by class, then MAX/MIN look inside each pile.

  • Without GROUP BY, SELECT MAX(MARK) FROM STUDENT gives one value for the whole table.
  • GROUP BY CLASS gives one row per class.
  • Group by several fields: GROUP BY CLASS, SEX.
  • Fields in SELECT should be grouped fields or aggregates.
  • Sort groups: ORDER BY MAX(MARK) DESC.

Exam wording: "GROUP BY groups records with the same value so that aggregate functions are computed for each group."
cards.zh:
直觉：GROUP BY 先按班分堆，MAX/MIN 再在每堆里找。

  • 不分组：整个表一个值。GROUP BY CLASS：每班一行。
  • SELECT 里只放分组 field 或汇总函数。

ex.q: Highest and lowest mark of each class.
ex.a:
1. SELECT CLASS, MAX(MARK) AS HI, MIN(MARK) AS LO FROM STUDENT GROUP BY CLASS.
  2. 5A: 85/78; 5B: 62/62 (NULL ignored); 5C: 91/49.

ex.q: Tallest student height for each sex.
ex.a:
1. SELECT SEX, MAX(HEIGHT) FROM STUDENT GROUP BY SEX.
  2. F: 163; M: 180.

ex.q: A student writes SELECT CLASS, CNAME, MAX(MARK) FROM STUDENT GROUP BY CLASS to get the top student's name. Problem?
ex.a:
1. CNAME is not grouped and not aggregated.
  2. Access gives an error; standard SQL does not allow it (SQLite just picks one row).
  3. Find the top mark first, then match names (a subquery), or list CLASS and MAX only.
ex.az: 1. CNAME 没分组也没汇总，Access 会报错。

code.src:
SELECT CLASS,
 MAX(MARK) AS HI,
 MIN(MARK) AS LO
FROM STUDENT
GROUP BY CLASS;

demo.query: SELECT CLASS, MAX(MARK) AS HI, MIN(MARK) AS LO FROM STUDENT GROUP BY CLASS;
demo.note: Each class becomes one row. 5B has only one non-NULL mark.

cards.en:
Intuition: WHERE checks each student at the door; HAVING checks each class pile after grouping.

  • COUNT(*) counts rows; COUNT(field) counts non-NULL values.
  • WHERE filters records before grouping; it cannot use aggregates.
  • HAVING filters groups after grouping; it uses aggregates like COUNT(*) > 1.
  • Boolean field: WHERE REGISTERED is enough (= TRUE is redundant).

Exam wording: "WHERE filters individual records before grouping, while HAVING filters groups after the aggregate is computed."
cards.zh:
直觉：WHERE 在门口逐个学生检查；HAVING 在分组后检查每一堆。

  • COUNT(*) 计行；COUNT(field) 计非 NULL。
  • WHERE 不能用汇总函数；HAVING 用于汇总后筛选。

ex.q: Number of students in each class.
ex.a:
1. SELECT CLASS, COUNT(*) AS NUM FROM STUDENT GROUP BY CLASS.
  2. 5A 2, 5B 2, 5C 2.

ex.q: Classes with at least 1 student scoring 80+.
ex.a:
1. Filter records first: WHERE MARK >= 80.
  2. Then group and keep groups: GROUP BY CLASS HAVING COUNT(*) >= 1.
  3. 5A (Lee Mei Ling), 5C (Amy Cheung).
ex.az: 1. 先 WHERE 再 GROUP BY … HAVING：5A、5C。

ex.q: Number of marks entered per class.
ex.a:
1. SELECT CLASS, COUNT(MARK) FROM STUDENT GROUP BY CLASS.
  2. 5A 2, 5B 1 (NULL skipped), 5C 2.

ex.q: A student writes SELECT CLASS FROM STUDENT WHERE COUNT(*) > 1 GROUP BY CLASS. Error?
ex.a:
1. Aggregates cannot be used in WHERE (WHERE runs before grouping).
  2. Correct: GROUP BY CLASS HAVING COUNT(*) > 1.

code.src:
SELECT CLASS, COUNT(*) AS NUM
FROM STUDENT
WHERE MARK >= 60
GROUP BY CLASS
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2;

notes.t: Step 1: keep only records with mark ≥ 60
notes.tz: 第一步：只留 ≥60 分的记录

notes.t: Step 3: keep classes with at least 2 such students → 5A
notes.tz: 第三步：只留至少 2 人的班 → 5A

code.out:
CLASS|NUM
5A|2

demo.query: SELECT CLASS, COUNT(*) AS NUM FROM STUDENT WHERE MARK >= 60 GROUP BY CLASS HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2;
demo.note: Remove the HAVING line to see all classes after WHERE.

cards.en:
Intuition: SUM adds the pile; AVG shares it out equally. An alias is the label on top of the answer column.

  • SUM(field): total. AVG(field): average. Both ignore NULL.
  • AS alias is optional, but with several summary columns it makes the result readable.

Exam wording: "AVG() ignores NULL values, so the average is calculated from records with a stored value only."
cards.zh: 直觉：SUM 是加总；AVG 是平分。别名（AS）是结果栏的标签。两者都忽略 NULL；有多个汇总栏时用别名较易读。

ex.q: Average mark of each sex.
ex.a:
1. SELECT SEX, AVG(MARK) AS AVGMARK FROM STUDENT GROUP BY SEX.
  2. F: (85+62+91)/3 = 79.33.
  3. M: (78+49)/2 = 63.5 (Ho Ka Lok's NULL ignored).

ex.q: Total height of 5C students.
ex.a:
1. SELECT SUM(HEIGHT) FROM STUDENT WHERE CLASS = '5C'.
  2. 180 + 163 = 343.

ex.q: A student says the boys' average is (78+0+49)/3 = 42.33 because Ho Ka Lok has no mark. Correct?
ex.a:
1. No. NULL is not 0; AVG ignores it.
  2. Average = (78+49)/2 = 63.5.

code.src:
SELECT SEX,
 SUM(HEIGHT) AS TOTAL_H,
 ROUND(AVG(MARK), 2) AS AVGMARK
FROM STUDENT
GROUP BY SEX;

notes.tz: 平均分（忽略 NULL），2 位小数

code.out:
SEX|TOTAL_H|AVGMARK
F|478|79.33
M|520|63.5

demo.query: SELECT SEX, SUM(HEIGHT) AS TOTAL_H, AVG(MARK) AS AVGMARK FROM STUDENT GROUP BY SEX;
demo.note: M average is 63.5, not 42.33: NULL is skipped.

cards.t: Order of evaluation: WHERE → GROUP BY → aggregate
cards.tz: 执行次序：WHERE → GROUP BY → 汇总
cards.en:
Intuition: a summary query is a production line. Each station does one job, always in the same order.

  1. FROM: take the table.
  2. WHERE: keep or drop each record.
  3. GROUP BY: put remaining records into groups.
  4. Aggregate: SUM/COUNT/AVG... for each group.
  5. HAVING: keep or drop groups.
  6. ORDER BY: sort the result.

Example (FOODMENU): SELECT MEALSET, SUM(PRICE) FROM FOODMENU WHERE NOT (FOODTYPE = 'Side Dish' AND PRICE < 20) GROUP BY MEALSET

Exam wording: "Records are first filtered by WHERE, then grouped, then the aggregate function is applied to each group."
cards.zh: 直觉：汇总查询是生产线，每站做一件事，次序固定：FROM → WHERE（逐个记录）→ GROUP BY → 汇总 → HAVING（逐组）→ ORDER BY。

ex.q: Trace the FOODMENU example.
ex.a:
1. WHERE: drop Side Dish under $20 → Chicken Nugget (16) and French Fries (14) removed. (Salad 24 and Soup 20 stay.)
  2. Group A: Burger 30, Cola 10, Salad 24 → 64.
  3. Group B: Fish Fillet 20, Tea 10 → 30.
  4. Group C: Rice 25, Soup 20, Juice 8 → 53.

ex.q: Add HAVING SUM(PRICE) > 50. Which sets remain?
ex.a:
1. HAVING runs after the sums: A 64, B 30, C 53.
  2. Keep > 50: A and C.

ex.q: A student first groups and sums (A 80, B 44, C 53) and then removes the cheap side dishes from the totals. Same answer?
ex.a:
1. Here yes by luck, but the method is wrong: WHERE always acts on records before grouping.
  2. With HAVING or COUNT the wrong order gives different results (e.g. COUNT(*) would be 4, 3, 3 instead of 3, 2, 3).
ex.az: 1. 方法错：WHERE 一定在分组前作用于记录；用 COUNT 时结果就不同。

code.src:
SELECT MEALSET, SUM(PRICE) AS TOTAL
FROM FOODMENU
WHERE NOT (FOODTYPE = 'Side Dish' AND PRICE < 20)
GROUP BY MEALSET;

notes.t: Show set and its total price
Drop each cheap side dish first
Then group and sum each set

code.out:
MEALSET|TOTAL
A|64
B|30
C|53

demo.note: Highlighted rows are kept by WHERE; then each meal set is summed.

ex.a:
1. SELECT CLASS, AVG(MARK) AS A FROM STUDENT GROUP BY CLASS HAVING AVG(MARK) > 70 ORDER BY A DESC.
  2. 5A 81.5, 5C 70 is not > 70 → only 5A.

ex.q: Count girls in each class.
ex.a:
1. SELECT CLASS, COUNT(*) FROM STUDENT WHERE SEX = 'F' GROUP BY CLASS.
  2. 5A 1, 5B 1, 5C 1.

ex.q: A student writes SELECT * FROM STUDENT ORDER BY MARK GROUP BY CLASS. Fix the clause order.
ex.a:
1. GROUP BY must come before ORDER BY, and SELECT should list only group fields/aggregates.
  2. E.g. SELECT CLASS, MAX(MARK) FROM STUDENT GROUP BY CLASS ORDER BY MAX(MARK).
ex.az: 1. GROUP BY 要在 ORDER BY 前。

demo.note: Try changing 70 to 60.

mc.q: Which of the following best describes a database?
o: A set of rules for formatting text
A program that performs calculations in cells
A collection of structured data stored in a computer system that facilitates storage and retrieval
mc.e: Definition of database.
mc.ez: 数据库是有结构、方便储存和检索的数据集合。

mc.q: Which of the following is NOT a database management system?
mc.e: PowerPoint is presentation software.

mc.q:
Which of the following are features provided by a DBMS?
(1) Changing the database schema
(2) Retrieval of data through searching
(3) Providing an interface for other programs to access the data
mc.e: All three are DBMS features listed in the book.
